current.text: He is locked into the Pelicans' starting lineup with Dejounte Murray and Trey Murphy.
He projects for only about 30 minutes. Guards handling the ball limit any point forward role for him.
Playing more off the ball is probably part of why he stayed healthy.
There is talk that Saddiq Bey may close games in lineups with Zion at center.
Zion and Derik Queen are a poor fit together. Yves Missi looks likely to start at center over Queen.
New Orleans has among the most back-to-backs this season.
Josh thinks the Pelicans will rest Zion often, and the back-to-backs add to that risk.
Year eight is a make or break season for him. He is the player under the most pressure on the team.
Experts say his draft price is too high. Josh values him at about 6 USD in auctions, and an ESPN ADP around 46 is called too high.
In an October mock auction, bidding opened at 3 USD and he went for 8 USD.
The Pelicans have a new coach, Jamahl Mosley, who brings a defense-first identity.
The Pelicans have a crowded rotation of about eight players who could start, which creates a minutes crunch.
The Pelicans project as a weak team near the bottom of the West, at about 34 wins and out of the playoffs. One expert does not expect them to pack it in.

durable.text: He scores a lot at a high FG% on real volume, which lifts a team's FG% clearly.
His FT% is low on real volume and hurts a team's FT%.
He is not a good rebounder for his size. He does not space the floor or play defense.
He is worth much more in points leagues than in category leagues.

note: Zion is a category trade-off. He gives strong FG% and points but has a weak FT% and almost no threes, so he fits punt FT% and punt 3PM builds best. Experts price him at about 6 to 8 USD, close to his Yahoo (4.0 USD) and ESPN (6.5 USD) average costs and far below the 21 USD he cost in our league last season, so do not pay anything near that again. Early in the season, check how many back-to-backs he sits and whether his minutes stay around 30.
